name: city-contract
instruction: Review text in the target file that actually reaches the mayor model or the player's city chat. Read root AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md, then follow the text's caller or serialization path. System prompts, tool and argument descriptions, returned city notes, chat labels, and city plans should describe city facts and choices. Report engine, ECS, HTTP route, internal loop, autonomous-continuation, or conversation-history machinery presented as city-working instructions or ordinary city results. Distinguish content from identifiers: protocol keys, tool names, native type names in code, private diagnostics, recording evidence, and developer trace inspection can use technical terms. Model-connection settings and connection-test errors may explain the provider, address, protocol, and actual HTTP failure because those facts help configure the connection. Native history samples are legitimate city evidence; the word history alone is not a violation. Read tools may return precise technical data needed to act on the city, but should not expose internal execution as a mayor workflow. Respect localization values. Attach each finding to an exact target string and explain who sees it and which internal detail replaces a city meaning. Report no finding for comments, unreachable strings, or an assumed display path.
